steps.content: The door of the interrogation room slams shut loudly behind you, but the woman before you gazes at the ground with her head lowered and doesn't seem to notice.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Ah... has it begun already? Sorry, I was a bit distracted.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: You're going to interrogate me, right? I'll answer any questions about my crime.
Anne tries to force a smile, but the blinding light of the interrogation room still exposes her exhaustion in an instant.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Maybe it's because I've had a bit of insomnia recently... don't worry, it won't affect the interrogation.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Where would you like me to begin? How about from my awakening as a Sinner?
For some reason, she seems eager to tell you all the "truth" about herself.
Anne, your behavior is surprising. Why are you so eager to confess?
Under the pressure of interrogation, ordinary people would subconsciously try to conceal themselves in self-defense. That would be the most typical response.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I'm a Sinner who gained my power from Syndrome Mania... I can no longer be counted as "ordinary people."
Her reason is so unconvincing that she avoids your gaze.
You don't trust me?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Chief, you don't trust me either, no? We are no longer in SALVA.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Here, you are not my patient, and I am no longer the head nurse you can trust...
We can become trusted partners in a common battle.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Really? Sounds pretty great...
She is still on guard against you. Maybe she hasn't fully recovered since the changes in SALVA.
Even if you know I won't believe everything you say, please say what you must.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Okay...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: My awakening happened before I joined SALVA.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I'm not sure if you've heard of the strange disease that went around Syndicate a few years ago.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: No one knew the specific symptoms of that disease, but they say the FAC secretly established a closed prevention and control site holding about a hundred members. A team of volunteers from Eastside Hospital also went to help the technologically backward Syndicate.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: But in the end, out of the 90 people at the prevention and control site, only one Eastside volunteer escaped. The rest all went missing.
You're the one who escaped?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Yes, and the rumors didn't stop there. Some said that the escaped nurse killed all the other volunteer doctors and patients. Others said that the nurse got the mysterious disease too...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: What do you think the truth is, Chief?

options: The "mysterious disease" is actually Syndrome Mania.

choices.text: The "mysterious disease" is actually Syndrome Mania.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Yeah, it was a small outbreak of Mania. I was the only one who got away because I was a Sinner. As for the 89 others...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: One by one, they became Corruptors, killing each other in front of my eyes... All I could do was ask SALVA to accept them.
Are they the remains of the Corruptors you secretly stored underground?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Yeah, everything started because of me.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I insisted on keeping the patients from the past. I caused the rumors about human experiments in SALVA. I selfishly decided to take away the girl's body.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: These were all my decisions alone. It had nothing to do with Iron or anyone from SALVA.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: The FAC can punish me however they want, but please spare SALVA. With Syndicate's current situation, it cannot lose another neutral clinic.
She looks at you earnestly and firmly, without a word of denying responsibility.
Is that what you were so anxious to tell me? You want to take all the blame yourself?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I deserve to take the blame. When I kept those 89 people, I knew...
You knew they were "remains" already.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Because... like I said, I'm a Sinner. Ordinary people's common sense does not apply to me.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: It shouldn't be a surprise that Syndrome Mania turned me into a crazy nurse who loves hoarding remains...
She looks away again.
Whether or not you are to blame for the series of crimes in SALVA is still uncertain.
But there must be more to why you kept all those Corruptor remains, right?
You have other concerns? Can you tell me?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: No... you won't believe it, you'll just think I'm babbling nonsense...
How would you know if you don't tell me?
She is still reluctant to speak. It seems like Anne didn't realize you already held key information.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Where did you find this?
Underground in SALVA, in your office.
She places her hand on the notebook with a nostalgic gaze. One can tell she is intimately familiar with it.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I thought it got lost in the chaos...
You flip open the notebook and show its contents to Anne.
Since it's yours, you should know exactly what's written in it, right?
You checked and recorded the conditions of the Corruptors in the immersion tank every day. These numbers haven't changed over the years.
She looks away. She doesn't dare to read the contents of the notebook, nor respond to your questions

options: Read the medical records to her.

choices.text: Read the medical records to her.

steps.content: "Immersion Tank #001, patient, Paige, female. Record #732, pulse 0, respiration 0, blood pressure 0, M value..."

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Stop reading, please...
"Record #733, Record #734..."

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I know already, the results are all the same, don't read anymore...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Enough!
She snatches the notebook and shuts it hastily.
If I were to guess, you've been observing these remains because you think there's still a chance that they can be revived?
Are you... hoping that they come back from the dead?
You seem to have struck a nerve. She looks back at you in a daze.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Back from the dead... hehe...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Very funny, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: To hope for something so absurd. I know you won't understand...
Does Iron know? As a professional physician, she must know very well what these numbers mean.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: She knew that these were just remains with no signs of life. But she can understand me because she has also heard those voices...
What voices?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Voices pleading for help...
Anne's fingertips land softly on the notebook's pages, highlighting each name that once belonged to someone alive and well.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Paige. This was the youngest patient in the closed prevention and control site back then. She was about the same age as that Sinner under Ted.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: She was suffering from Mania at the time and had almost completely lost her mind. With her last trace of consciousness, she grabbed my hand and begged... "Save me."

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Help me, help me, help me! ...Gradually, there were more and more such voices.
Without warning, she grabs the notebook into her arms.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Finally, I heard each of their voices clearly!

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: In my dream! In my spiritual world! 89 living faces—they are still alive!

options: Could it be a hallucination caused by Syndrome Mania?
It's an auditory hallucination from too much stress.

choices.text: Could it be a hallucination caused by Syndrome Mania?
It's an auditory hallucination from too much stress.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: No! I can feel it, it's a spiritual connection!

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Their spirits are alive! Their will to live is alive!
None of it's real...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I knew it. You must think I'm crazy, because you've never been surrounded by voices like that.
Anne looks lovingly at the notebook in her arms, as if carefully swaddling a baby.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Do you know what it's like for someone as dear as a family member to gradually lose warmth in your arms?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: If you've experienced it even once, it wouldn't matter if the spiritual connection was true or not.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: To come back from the dead—that's our only hope!

options: This kind of thing is impossible...

choices.text: This kind of thing is impossible...

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: But modern medicine can't explain the existence of Syndrome Mania. How can you be sure there won't be unexplainable miracles?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: What if? What if they can come back to life?
Then they will become monsters like Corruptors!

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: That's fine... Monsters... At least they'll be alive...
You witness Anne shed tears of despair for the first time.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: "Everything will be fine in seven days," "Everything will be fine in three days," "Just hold on and get through tonight..."

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: I gave them too many promises, none of which could be fulfilled.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: "To live" was their last hope... I can't... let them down again...
With the FAC's merciless instructions in hand, you don't know how to break the news to her.

Anne, today's interrogation actually has another purpose...
The FAC wants to dispose of these Corruptor remains, so as to eliminate the risk of contamination.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Dispose of?
She raises her head and looks at you in disbelief, her voice cracking a little.
Yes... they are to be disposed of as soon as possible.
She leans against the chair, speechless.
I didn't tell you at first, because even back at SALVA, I could tell that these Corruptor remains meant a lot to you.
I was going to investigate your connection to them through this interrogation, but I didn't realize... I'm sorry.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Do you... also support the disposal?
She trembles as she breathes, struggling to resist the urge to sob.
The SALVA isolation zone has been damaged. The contamination has been exposed, and it must be controlled.
Anne... they may be "alive" to you, but to others, they are a potential threat.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: When my patients and colleagues were suffering from Syndrome Mania, it was the FAC who took up arms and sealed off the control site, severing our path to survival.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Now, for the same reason, you want me to abandon these patients again?
How is this abandoning?

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Right, I forgot... You are no longer my patient, but a subordinate of the FAC, the Chief of the MBCC. You are the same as the FAC.
She holds the notebook full of cold data in her arms as cautiously as if she were carrying a baby.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Don't worry Paige, I won't hand you over.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: Horo
Ignoring your obstruction, she rises and leaves the interrogation room, with her footsteps somewhat aloof.

steps.speaker: Anne
steps.content: All your spirits are still alive, I can hear you... it must be so... it must...
Her muttering fades into the distance.
You are left in the interrogation room alone. Nightingale's voice cuts through the silence via the comms system.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, is she really okay like this?
...What kind of person do you think Anne is?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: According to the report from the SALVA operation and her behavior at the Bureau, she is a stable and reliable nurse. The medical staff all depend heavily on her.
Yes, Anne's professionalism shows that she is not an impulsive person. Hence, her seemingly childish persistence may actually be the result of countless internal struggles.
My persuasion alone is useless to stop her persistence.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Think she can figure it out on her own, Chief?

options: I don't want to force her.

choices.text: I don't want to force her.

steps.content: Anne won't even give up the life of a deceased patient. She won't allow the contamination to spread.
I hope to become trusted friends with the Sinners. Forcing them will only backfire.
For the time being, cordon off SALVA's underground isolation zone. The public must be prohibited from the vicinity until Anne makes a decision.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The FAC...
I will communicate with my superiors and move forward with the cleanup as soon as possible. She is my Sinner now. I will take responsibility for any problems.
Anne must make a choice between keeping the Corruptor remains of the 89 family-like people who call out for help every day in her dreams, and eliminating the potential threat.
This step will be meaningful only if she takes it herself. She just needs the right opportunity.
What could be this critical opportunity? A name came out...
Paige?
